objective: Prove: (1) an isotropy principle: if a space of plane tilings with finite local complexity up to rigid motions is invariant under rotations and uniquely ergodic under translations, then for almost every tiling the bond distance of any parity law placed on it by a rigid-motion-covariant rule, divided by distance, tends to one constant in every direction; (2) hence the pinwheel's parity laws (knots at tile corners; knots on tiles) have exactly round circles, a distance that counts distinctions and uses no lengths; (3) the same substitution with legs 1:1 gives the periodic tetrakis triangulation, whose laws have polygonal circles with rational pi (10/3 and 4); (4) legs 1:m with m >= 2 turn tiles through arctan(1/m), an irrational multiple of pi (Niven), and a ball of radius R meets only O(log R) orientations, so roundness is a large-scale trend. Check the substitutions, the lemmas and the bounds by computation.
status: Proved (PINWHEEL-ROUND-20261107-001A-P001), conditional on Radin's cited theorems: isotropy makes logical circles round. If a tiling space with finite local complexity is rotation-invariant and uniquely ergodic under translations, every rigid-motion-covariant bond distance with linear bounds is round. So the pinwheel's parity laws (knots at corners; knots on tiles) have exactly round circles, a distance that counts distinctions and uses no lengths (Radin and Sadun had shown it for Euclidean edge length). The same 1:2 triangle cut frame-consistently keeps one frame, and the 1:1 triangle's substitution is the periodic tetrakis triangulation, with polygonal circles (pi = 10/3, 4): roundness needs an irrational angle and tiles of both handednesses. A disc of radius R meets O(log R) orientations: roundness is a large-scale trend.
title: Isotropy makes logical circles round: the pinwheel law
